Params: Wake up. Come on, wake up.
Don't let the ocean take you.
You jolt awake from your nightmare, the sheets drenched in cold sweat.
The cabin rocks violently, like a cradle tossed about by the storm.
The ocean threatens to tear the world apart outside your window. Whirlpools spiral into a chasm, and the mounting waves threaten to bring doom.
In your dream, Karenina was walking along a desolate shore.
You chased after her, but she remained several meters ahead, no matter how hard you tried.
The laws of physics twisted and warped in that grotesque world...
Until Karenina stopped at a cliff's edge, where waves break at her feet like shattered glass flowers.
Chants of chaos drifted through the air, mingled with the wails of young dying beasts.
She turned back and smiled at you, and in that instant, every cell in your body screamed in terror.
Commandant... you idiot... you really are...
She fell from the cliff, and you dove after her without thinking.
Wind hammered your eardrums like bullets, the pain piercing and relentless.
The instant your fingers touched Karenina's, the world exploded with a deafening bang.
Gray was the sky, white was the shore, blue was the ocean, and red... was your blood.
Shards of the world flew upward, assaulting you from all sides.
The churning whirlpool opened its gaping maw, waiting to swallow Karenina whole.
You wrench yourself back to reality from the nightmare, but your mind remains in disarray.
Stumbling through the corridors to the central deck, you find others also roused by the storm. They gather in small clusters, trying to pass the sleepless hours.
Swaying overhead lights cast harsh glares across poker games and barrels of whiskey. Cooling the liquor are chunks of ice worth more than the alcohol itself.
Did you hear? Another Construct defected.
What is it this time? This place feels cursed... people just vanish every so often.
Maybe lured away by mermaids or something.
The kind of mermaid that grows fangs in the middle of the night? Yeah, I'll pass on that. But hey, if you're into it, knock yourself out.
Can you get me a line to Babylonia?
I'm not approving a requisition just because you had a nightmare. That's absurd.
And it's not just me. Anyone with half a brain would refuse.
"The Reciprocal Influence Between M.I.N.D. Dream Architecture and Folk Mythologies"? That's got to be the most outlandish research topic I've heard all year.
So what you really want is a ship.
You'd better hope there really is some remarkable sunken city like Heracleion underneath the outpost.
Otherwise, all that nonsense you spouted isn't worth a single brick from a lost ruin.
Asimov continues his fearsome monologue on the other end of the call, before pausing at the end.
Karenina had to swap frames in a rush for that Atlantic mission... The authorization process was sloppy to begin with, and she didn't get the recovery time she needed afterward.
So I want you to confirm she's functioning properly. With that in mind, I'll vouch for your operation... but not because of that outlandish theory of yours.
You care about your colleagues so much.
Don't overthink it. Any research data on the Nexus frame matters greatly to the Science Council. I just need to make sure things stay on track.
(And of course, every person... matters greatly too.)
Asimov cuts the call before finishing his thought, and he dives back into his work.

At least you do manage to secure an emergency boat and a brief window of free time. As you leave the main vessel, the lifeboat that has been sent to retrieve you surfaces from the water like a magic trick.
The journey to the outpost is long, and rain hammers relentlessly against the hull. The helmsman glances back at his "passenger" with "concern."
Happens all the time to people who haven't gotten their sea legs yet. Eight out of ten go through it.
Come to think of it, isn't Babylonia technically a ship too? You'd think people from there would do better.
Hey, don't sweat it. They say dreams are just reality bleeding through, no? That's how people on land get prophetic dreams all the time.
But out here on the ocean? Everything's flipped. The rules don't work the same way out here... It's a whole different world.
So whoever you dreamed about is probably fast asleep, having the best dream ever.
You notice "The King in Yellow" propped against the helmsman's sonar terminal and sign, deciding to ignore his comfort.
Sorry for dragging you out at this hour.
Who doesn't love working the graveyard shift?
Surprises, accidents, drama, chaos... it's all wonderfully miraculous.
The storm's going to ground everything for the next day or two, so no ships will be leaving port. We'll hold your berth till you're back safe.
But I do know a thing or two more than you when it comes to the sea, so I've got no choice but to give you my "blessing."
For the Deep Ones, they venture into that world searching for things that don't exist in reality.
But by the time they realize they've been deceived, there's no turning back—they've already sprouted gills, tendrils, things like that. They've become monsters.
So whether it's you or the person you're looking for, remember: no matter how close to the abyss you find yourself and how desperate things get...
Always be ready to <color=#ff4e4eff>pull yourself out</color>. Human or Construct, we all belong in the real world.
Alright, we're approaching your destination. Please gather your belongings and prepare to disembark. And if there's a feedback survey, I'd appreciate a five-star rating.
You notice his name came from the badge on his uniform, but... something about it feels off.
Still mulling over his cryptic words, you arrive at the temporary outpost as the sun rises.
The dawning sun shifts in unpredictable brilliance. Crimson red bleeds into radiant gold over mere seconds before settling into familiar, comforting warmth.
The freak weather raged through the night, but aside from a few fish washed ashore by the waves, nothing else has suffered any damage.
7:40 AM\nConference Room, Atlantic Temporary Outpost, Earth
The moment you reach the conference room, heated voices drift through the door.
At least there's a familiar voice in the mix—Karenina sounds fine.
What?! What do you mean "she can't take any pressure"?!
Tch! She is clearly absconding, that's what it is! Her evaluation's just days away!
And now you're telling me she pulled a disappearing act?!
At least things haven't gotten unsalvageable yet.
Sure, you're not wrong! But do you have any idea how hard it is to bring a qualified intern through to full-time in the Engineering Force?
First, the candidate needed to last at least three summers in an internship at the Cosmos Technicians Union before getting recommended to the Engineering Force by a mentor.
Then, there are written exams, interviews, cross-functional interviews, personality tests, interview panels, and a whole year of daily apprenticeship before the evaluation exam!
Calling it "daily apprenticeship" is putting it lightly. It's more like a full-time job with no breaks...
Come to think of it, I didn't expect you to pay this much attention to intern recruitment.
I've gone through tons of applications and reports, so how could I not notice? You don't seriously think I just rubber-stamp everything with my eyes closed, do you?
Karenina lowers her voice suddenly as if talking to herself, before speaking normally again.
Truth is, working in the Engineering Force isn't exactly a walk in the park, no matter how cheerful everyone acts.
The workload's relentless, every little mistake gets blown up in your face, and when you're on the clock, you're really on the clock. There's no fancy training program to speak of.
Mm... You could say it's a complete mess.
That's exactly why we have to bring her back!
I don't care if it's Xoth, or Hoth, or somewhere worse... I'll drag her back myself. Whatever's going on can wait until after the evaluation.
Perhaps she just doesn't want to stay with the Engineering Force anymore, and she'd be better off somewhere else. Maybe the Cosmos Technicians Union?
Or the secondary departments in the Science Council that handle engineering logistics? They like hiring people with technical knowledge and clerical skills.
Mika can't help but smile bitterly while listing these options, knowing full well how much Kiki loves the Engineering Force and how hard she's worked to stay there...
Karenina leans back in her chair and lets out a long sigh, her hands pressed against the back of her head as she mulls something over.
Nah. Those places are alright, but they weren't her first choice.
"To become the best engineer, surpassing even Instructor Karenina (and Instructor Teddy)." That's what Kiki wrote under Career Goals on her application.
The thing is, even when she's given her all, she's only middling compared to her peers.
Ambitious? What do you think it takes for a researcher to go the distance, Mika?
Karenina shakes her head, her expression far more serious than usual.
Actually, I think it's ambition. Any engineering researcher who's been selected to work on Babylonia must be really talented already.
Engineering research isn't easy. It requires so much fieldwork and lab work, and the standards are sky-high. When a room is full of geniuses, ability alone can't determine who comes out on top.
It's the all-or-nothing, never-back-down mentality—you must finish the race, surpass everyone else, and never give up.
Everyone pursues their ambitions differently, but at the end of the day, you'll never make it to the finish line without that drive.
I never knew you could think this profoundly.
Hey! I'm standing right here! I've got ears!
Watching Karenina bristle like that, Mika knows she never has to worry about her captain.
So, Captain, do you think she'll succeed?
Honestly? I don't know for sure. But I believe she can.
She used to be this bright, cheerful kid. A year later, she had dark circles under her eyes, and her hair was so greasy you couldn't tell the last time she washed it.
She wouldn't say a word all day, and she'd run off to the Star of Life for the tiniest thing: headaches, stomach problems, insomnia, you name it.
She joined the Engineering Force with a dream and put in all that effort. Now she's going to throw it all away and run when she's this close to the finish line?
I won't let that happen! I'll turn this place upside down to bring her back...
The door swings open just as Karenina finishes speaking, and the two of them turn around in unison.
Karenina's expression shifts from surprise to delight, and she braces against the desk to stand up. Then, realizing how eager she looks, she sits back down.
I'm requesting to join the mission to find the missing intern.
Oh, it's the Gray Raven Commandant.
I feel better about letting the captain go if you're joining her...
Hey, I haven't agreed to this yet! Don't act like it's already decided!
And Mika, you've been worried that I can't handle this on my own this whole time, haven't you!
And one more thing, Commandant—just how long were you standing outside that door?
Aren't you on a mission? Is something wrong?
<size=31>(Explain the situation without the part about the nightmare)</size>
You tell Karenina that the storm has forced your ship to anchor temporarily, and that Asimov happened to ask you to check on how she is adapting to her new frame.
Everything you said is true, except for the part about the nightmare... Telling her about it now would only make her worry.
Anyway, I'll leave her to you. There's still a lot of work at the outpost that needs my support. I'm going to head over there now.
After explaining the basics, Mika shoves the files into your hands and smoothly heads toward the door.
You can feel the dust Mika kicks up while jogging away even from where you stand.
If you want to go it alone, Karenina...
She leaps from her seat—too late to catch Mika, but just in time to get right in your face.
I mean, look, I can handle this by myself just fine, but since you're offering... I guess I have to let you tag along.
Fair warning: this mission's way more of a hassle than usual. We're talking diving, weird rumors, and maybe even a little danger.
She suddenly recalls something as she says that. Digging into her pocket, she pulls out a pendant and holds it up right in front of your face.
The pendant is a miniaturized replica of Karenina's anchor weapon, meticulously polished and gleaming silver.
Actually, you could just wait for me back at the outpost with this tracker. If something does happen, you can use this to come find me.
Yeah. I've been meaning to give this to you for a while now, but I kept getting swamped with work, and it slipped my mind.
Just keep it safe, okay? I only made one of these, and you're the only one I'm sharing the anchor access with.

You take the pendant and carefully secure it close to your body. The raised metal plate rests against your chest, and the anchor sits right over your heart, quietly transmitting Karenina's coordinates.
Seeing you do this, Karenina shows an expression of relief, as if she has finally finished something she prepared for a long time.
So... does this mean you agree?
Huh? I thought we agreed you'd wait for me back at the outpost, didn't we?
I can't just sit around while my friend goes into danger alone.
Karenina's eyes widen, her expression shifting from surprise to irritation as she plants her hands on her hips.
Hmph! I see what this is. You just wanted to trick me to give you my tracker!
She doesn't bother to reply. Grabbing your arm, she drags you straight to the equipment room, blunt as ever.
11:40 AM\nAbandoned Underwater Base, Atlantic Ocean, Earth
The floor at the offshore outpost is scorching in mid-August, the air thick and heavy. The moment you step out of the air-conditioned room, you start feeling stressed.
But the moment you hit the water, it all vanishes without a trace.
The ocean floor is another world entirely, one that harbors all life forms, both dead and evolved, since time immemorial. It is both a womb and a tomb.
After diving for some time, the two of you follow Kiki's last signal to an abandoned underwater base.
Karenina raises her scanner and sweeps the area before nodding at you and confirming this is the place. Together, you go deeper inside.
A collapsed signpost half-buried in the silt lies unnoticed, the words on it corroded beyond recognition: <color=#ff4e4eff>Xoth, Binary Star</color>.
Do you feel it too...? This creeping unease? The deeper we go, the worse it gets.
Like someone... or something... is watching us from the other side.
Karenina brushes at her shoulder as she speaks, as if trying to shake off the invisible eyes watching her.
The feeling of being watched... There is a theory that when a being is observed, neurons in the brain detect it first and send out a warning, known colloquially as a         "sixth sense."
You don't admit that you feel it too. Instead, you just move a little closer to Karenina.
What would bring an intern to a place like this?
Maybe it's because she received that "signal." This place used to be one of the Copperfield family's entertainment ventures.
A "large-scale immersive scripted murder mystery experience"... they called it               "Jubensha" in the files.
They lured customers by sending out "signals" from the ocean depths to the mainland. It could be a will promising a massive inheritance, a strange letter, or even an unusual dream.
Recalling your bizarre dream, you only hope it wasn't part of the script. This immersive experience would be very terrifying otherwise.
There'd always be some who got curious after receiving the signal. They'd follow the clues here, activate the "script," experience the full story, and then leave.
A lot of things happened in Transatlantic later... Long story short, the project was discontinued, but the base kept transmitting those invitation signals.
If only it were that simple! By the time this base came up again in conversation, it was already years later.
A lot of people have disappeared here, then turned up back on land... but every single one came back broken. Humans with mental instability, and Constructs with their M.I.N.D.s damaged.
They even lost their memories of the facility, needing months of treatment just to become functional again.
Karenina shrugs and shakes her head, then takes a few quick steps forward before turning to face you, hands clasped behind her back as she continues her explanation.
For one thing, nobody actually died, and the disappearances happened sporadically.
And second, it wasn't high priority. There's always something more critical going down every day in our world.
Discussing the mission eases some of the oppressive atmosphere that's hung over you two since entering the facility.
As Karenina skips backward, mechanoids buried beneath the mud and sand lurch stiffly to their feet behind her.
One, two... too many to count.
You grab Karenina and pull her back just in time. Judging by their appearance, you are certain that these mechanoids have been infected by the Punishing Virus.
But they show no further hostility or reaction to the intruders before them after they rise.
They simply shamble about on their own, endlessly reliving the sorrows of days long past like spirits haunting a graveyard.
I found "work," didn't I? We weren't going to be hungry anymore, right?
I promised you we'd move to a room with a window after I get paid. You'd be able to see the roses then, and you wouldn't feel so stifled anymore.
Why didn't you trust me? Why, Aria? We came here to escape a disaster...
But why... why did we end up becoming each other's disaster?
The Corrupted mechanoid clutches his abdomen and collapses, seemingly trying to staunch his bleeding wound. After convulsing for a while, he falls still once more.

He sinks back into the mud and sand, leaving only a dagger behind. It is a combat knife commonly found in conservation areas, renowned for its durability and versatility. Even now, it is considered valuable currency.
Karenina crouches down to pick it up, tucking it away after a few wipes.
There's a name on this. Maybe we can find whoever it belonged to when we bring it back.
Yeah, I know it's a long shot, but... I can't leave it here.
A small hand pats her on her shoulder, and Karenina jumps, startled.
The child mechanoid claps and spins away, clearly pleased with his prank. After putting some distance between Karenina and himself, he stops and begins making taunting gestures.

Your mood fluctuates like the needle on the virus detector. Punishing Virus concentration has been dropping as you get closer to the base, which means there must be some kind of purification system inside.

The source of the Punishing Virus here is impossible to trace. It could have accumulated on the seabed, or leaked from the mainland. Either way, something happened here that never saw the light of day.
If you weren't here, Commandant, I'd have beaten him up by now.
Readings look fine. Let's follow it.
The mechanoid toys with you two effortlessly, darting back and forth, appearing and vanishing like a shadow, like a well-fed cat toying with its prey.
Eventually, he stops beside a female Corrupted. Only her upper body protrudes from the ground, as she hums a hauntingly beautiful melody.
She stops singing when you approach. Covering her face with her hands, she starts making sharp, twisted sounds of sobs and laughter.
Carcosa... summoned... song of true love... Hahaha... Liar, liar, liar...
This feels familiar. Is Scarlet Revelation here?
Without warning, the Corrupted flails her arms wildly and lunges at Karenina, like a drowning victim grasping for anything within reach.
Karenina stumbles back in panic, her foot catching a loose stone slab. She slips, falling straight into a trap that has been waiting for her.
There is no time to think. Grabbing her hand, you jump in after her. Meanwhile, the child mechanoid tilts his head and waves at you both at the edge of the trap.
My name's Patches! Don't forget it, yeah? Patches!
